clue.text: Big news story — sad end of space flight

parts.note: a splash is a newspaper's front-page lead story
feeling down means feeling sad

explanation.surface: A headline story mourning a mission that has just finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsule ending its mission by landing in the sea is the classic close of a crewed space trip.

clue.text: Rare blemish on church

parts.note: a scar is a mark or blemish
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An unusual mark on a church building.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something in short supply or seldom found.

clue.text: Like a wild animal at university, interrupting row

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of something, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a line is a row
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A beast loose on campus breaks up a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel but means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things wolf-like, wolves being wild animals.

clue.text: Learning gossip when drunk — with this?

definitions.text: Learning gossip when drunk — with this?

indicators.note: drunk means muddled, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Picking up rumours after too many cocktails, perhaps because of this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the drink is what might leave you gossiping.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin-based cocktail created at Raffles Hotel, the kind of drink that loosens tongues.

clue.text: Go out with actor Terence — one might make an impression

parts.note: to date someone is to go out with them
Terence Stamp is an English film actor

explanation.surface: A fan dreaming of a night out with a famous actor who would leave a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: This office device inks a date onto paper, literally pressing a mark there.

clue.text: Stick a fish in film?

parts.note: a wand is a thin stick

explanation.surface: Sticking a fish into a film scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The film is A Fish Called Wanda (1988); the question mark flags the indirect definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of a famous comedy is the one the title calls a fish.

clue.text: Get rid of outbuilding

definitions.meaning: to cast off, as a snake does its skin
a small hut in the garden for tools

explanation.surface: Clearing out the garden hut.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to discard, and the noun is a simple garden store; one word serves both.

clue.text: Pope's quality of verse read in High School initially

indicators.note: the verse goes in between the two initials
taking the first letter of each of the two words

parts.note: o' is a clipped of, as in man o' war
lines of poetry are read out

explanation.surface: Reciting a poem at school, judged on its saintly character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives H and S, and 'in' places O plus LINES between them.
explanation.definitionFit: The pope is addressed as His Holiness, sanctity being his defining quality.

clue.text: Is penny invested in stupid deal

indicators.note: clothed in, so the inner letters are wrapped by the other word

parts.note: dense means slow-witted

explanation.surface: Is a penny put into a foolish bargain?
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to deal out is to distribute or give out.

clue.text: PC operating system rarely seen nowadays

definitions.text: PC operating system rarely seen nowadays

parts.words: PC operating system rarely seen nowadays
parts.note: PC suggests a personal computer, but it is a police constable whose old way of operating, patrolling on foot, has nearly vanished

explanation.surface: An outdated computer operating system.
explanation.walkthrough: PC means police constable, not personal computer; the 'system' is the officer's method of patrolling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a police officer patrolling an area on foot, now uncommon.

clue.text: Snake with space on tree

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: A snake coiled with room to spare on a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: EN is a typesetting space, a measure the width of the letter N.
explanation.definitionFit: The quaking variety is a well-known poplar species.

clue.text: Bits of squid etc the French caught in net cast indiscriminately

indicators.note: something caught in a net sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other
cast any old how, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: A fisherman's net flung at random hauls in a squid and other sea creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast indiscriminately' makes TENTACS, and 'caught in' traps the French article inside it. 'etc' widens the squid to its relatives, octopus and cuttlefish.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid and octopus have long flexible limbs used for grasping prey.

clue.text: May see fool seek support

parts.note: may and can both mean being permitted
v. is short for vide, Latin for see
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: Perhaps a fool will spot the chance to look for backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month or a name but is the verb meaning 'is allowed to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidates go door to door soliciting votes, which is asking for backing.

clue.text: Consult expert about name in quizzical way

parts.note: to consult someone is to ask them

indicators.note: the expert's word goes about, or around, the letter for name

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Asking a specialist for advice about a name, with raised eyebrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking at someone sideways conveys doubt or suspicion, a questioning glance.

clue.text: Shopkeepers' basic cost not recovered

definitions.note: read as shopkeepers, with the apostrophe as surface glue

indicators.note: re-covered, i.e. covered again in a new way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Traders complaining that their basic outlay has not been recouped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recovered' looks like 'got back' but is read as 're-covered', signalling the jumble of BASIC COST NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: These traders run shops selling cigarettes, cigars and pipe supplies.

clue.text: List unusual clue to Aga

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list offering a strange hint about a kitchen range.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga is a heavy British range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic itemised record of goods or books is an inventory.

clue.text: Wonderful son flirting once

parts.note: mashing was an old slang word for flirting; 'once' marks it as dated

explanation.surface: A boy who used to be a terrific flirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British praise for something excellent or terrific.

clue.text: I call for help carrying most important electronic and nuclear materials

indicators.note: the distress call holds the other pieces within it

parts.note: SOS is the distress signal
top means foremost
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Someone shouting for help while lugging vital electronic and nuclear supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Variants of an element differing in neutron count are the stuff of nuclear physics.

clue.text: Dance from the 1960s made a hotspot delirious

indicators.note: wildly confused, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A sixties dance craze sends a nightclub hotspot into a frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1962 dance craze, named after a popular side dish, featured in a Dee Dee Sharp hit.

clue.text: Use craft to obtain foremost of white fish

indicators.note: the leading letter of the following word

parts.note: to angle is to fish with rod and line

explanation.surface: Using a boat to catch the best whitefish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests a boat but means cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something by guile or trickery is to contrive it slyly.

clue.text: Notice archdeacon on time for run-up to Christmas

parts.note: an ad is a notice
Ven, Venerable, is an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: An archdeacon posting a notice about Christmas preparations on time.
explanation.definitionFit: The church season of four Sundays leading up to the Nativity feast.

clue.text: Colonist taking dog round lake

indicators.note: the dog's word goes round the single letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a setter is a gun dog breed
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A pioneer walking a dog around a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes a new home in a newly founded colony is a pioneer resident.

clue.text: What may stop cricket broadcast as a rule

indicators.note: spoken over the air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: wet weather halts cricket matches

explanation.surface: As usual, a cricket match broadcast is halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as a rule' looks like 'usually' but 'as a' is a link and 'rule' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's period on the throne, or the act of governing, is their rule.

clue.text: Slippery type rejected protection, not being exposed

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the creature's name is written backwards

parts.note: an eel is proverbially slippery
ward means guard or protection, as in ward off

explanation.surface: A slippery character's offer of protection is turned down, keeping matters quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: The side sheltered from the wind is the side that is not exposed to it.

clue.text: Threatened one legislator with abolition

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws
abolition is the ending of something

explanation.surface: A lone lawmaker threatened with having the role scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjectival sense: something looming or about to happen is threatened, as a threatened storm.

clue.text: Bird of prey heading off hunting dog

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the dog's name is taken off

parts.note: a beagle is a hound bred for hunting hares

explanation.surface: A raptor flies away from a pursuing hound.
explanation.definitionFit: A large raptor with a hooked beak, the classic hunting bird.

clue.text: Cut fuel for heating hospital

parts.note: gas fuels many home boilers
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A hospital's heating fuel budget being slashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep wound or slash in skin is a noun synonym.

clue.text: Maybe shares how cleric is dressed for service

parts.note: dressed in robes, so the word in
a vestment is the robe a priest wears to conduct a service

explanation.surface: A description of a priest robing for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as IN VESTMENT: the cleric is clad 'in' a 'vestment'.
explanation.definitionFit: Buying stocks is one example of putting money to work for a return; 'Maybe' marks it as an example.
